problem.text: Consider a polynomial $p(x)$ of degree $1$ such that for a real number $a$, $p(a) = 2$, $p(p(a)) = 17$ and $p(p(p(a))) = 167$. What is the value of $a$?

steps.title: Where to start: unwrap the nested values
steps.body: A polynomial of degree $1$ has the form $p(x) = cx + d$ with $c \neq 0$, so we only need two numbers. The nested conditions look scary, but each one feeds in the value from the previous one: since $p(a) = 2$, the condition $p(p(a)) = 17$ says exactly that $p(2) = 17$.

your_turn.prompt: In the same way, rewrite $p(p(p(a))) = 167$ as a condition on $p$ at a plain number.

steps.title: Two equations for $c$ and $d$
steps.body:
Putting $x = 2$ and $x = 17$ into $p(x) = cx + d$ gives
$$2c + d = 17, \qquad 17c + d = 167$$
Both equations contain $d$ once, so subtracting them removes $d$.

your_turn.prompt: Subtract the equation $2c + d = 17$ from $17c + d = 167$. What is $c$?

steps.title: Find the whole polynomial
steps.body: Put $c = 10$ into $2c + d = 17$ to get $d = -3$. So $p(x) = 10x - 3$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Now use the first condition $p(a) = 2$: $10a - 3 = 2$, so $10a = 5$ and $a = \frac{1}{2}$. The answer is **(D)**.
